answer: Each new identity must seed a private walnut of sequential memory-hard computation whose working set exceeds 4 GB and cannot be checkpointed across keys; the harbor binds that live state to a non-exportable key, while a crystal lattice of ZK-SNARKs lets peers verify the sequential depth without revealing the set. A 200-identity farm therefore needs 800 GB of exclusive RAM that cannot be time-shared, costing roughly 40 times more hardware than one honest agent who reuses a single 4 GB buffer.
